title: Finite independent differential families remain independent in a geometrically regular local algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ be a Noetherian local $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with $K=A/\mathfrak m$, and suppose $A$ is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. For every finite index set $I$ and family $(a_i)_{i\in I}$ in $k$, if $(\mathrm da_i)_{i\in I}$ is linearly independent over $k$ in $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], then $(1\otimes\mathrm d(a_i\cdot1_A))_{i\in I}$ is linearly independent over $K$ in $K\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}$. The $\mathbf F_p$-algebra structure on $A$ is the composite through $k$. The empty family is included.

proof.text: If I is empty, independence is immediate. Otherwise enumerate I by Fin n. Use the trivial finite purely inseparable extension to obtain regularity of A and identify its conormal dimension d; the universe lift of k and tensor left-unit equivalence implement the trivial extension.

*The extension $k'$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-pth-roots-extension-degree] the subfield $k(a_1^{1/p},\dots,a_n^{1/p})$ of an algebraic closure of $k$ has degree $p^n$. Let $k'=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^p-a_1,\dots,x_n^p-a_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Using $x_j^p=a_j$, $k'$ is spanned over $k$ by the $p^n$ monomials $x^e$, $0\le e_j<p$, so $\dim_kk'\le p^n$; the $k$-algebra map $k'\to k(a_1^{1/p},\dots,a_n^{1/p})$, $x_j\mapsto a_j^{1/p}$, is surjective (its image $k[a_1^{1/p},\dots,a_n^{1/p}]$ is a field, being a domain finite over $k$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], and contains the generators). Comparing dimensions it is an isomorphism: $k'$ is a field with $[k':k]=p^n$. For $y=\sum_e\lambda_ex^e\in k'$, $y^p=\sum_e\lambda_e^pa^e\in k$ ($p$-th power is additive in characteristic $p$), so $k'/k$ is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular, line 8697), proof of (2) => (4) (lines 8789-8793): 'Consider the field extension k' = k(a_1^{1/p}, ..., a_n^{1/p}). By Algebra, Lemma 07DZ we see that k' = k[x_1, ..., x_n]/(x_1^p - a_1, ..., x_n^p - a_n)'

proof.text: *The ring $A'$ and its dimension.* Put $A'=A\otimes_kk'\cong A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(x_1^p-a_1,\dots,x_n^p-a_n)$ (tensoring the presentation of step 2 with $A$). By [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-base-change-local-ring]: $A\to A'$ is finite and free, $A'$ is a Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'$ is the only prime containing $\mathfrak mA'$, and $K'=A'/\mathfrak m'$ is a finite extension of $K$, with $A'/\mathfrak mA'\cong K\otimes_kk'$ finite dimensional over $K$. By geometric regularity [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] ($k'/k$ finite purely inseparable, step 2) $A'$ is regular, hence a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula] for the flat map $A\to A'$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $\mathfrak m'$ over $\mathfrak m$, $\dim A'=\dim A+\dim A'/\mathfrak mA'$; every prime of the finite-dimensional $K$-algebra $A'/\mathfrak mA'$ is maximal (a domain finite over $K$ is a field [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]), so $\dim A'/\mathfrak mA'=0$ and $\dim A'=d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] $\dim_{K'}\mathfrak m'/\mathfrak m'^2=d$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular, line 8697), proof of (3) => (1) (lines 8716-8750: 'A' is a local ring ... since A -> A' is finite flat we see that dim(A) = dim(A')') and proof of (2) => (4) ('By assumption A' is regular (and of the same dimension as A, see above)')

proof.text: *The map $\beta$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-pth-root-presentation-differentials] for $A$ and the images of $a_1,\dots,a_n$ in $A$: the sequence $A'^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{A'/A}\to0$, $\varepsilon(e_j)=1\otimes\mathrm da_j$, is exact and $\Omega_{A'/A}$ is free on $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$. Let $N=\operatorname{im}w=\ker z$. As $\Omega_{A'/A}$ is free, $0\to N\to\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{A'/A}\to0$ splits and stays exact after $-\otimes_{A'}K'$; and $A'^{\oplus n}\to A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\to N\to0$ stays exact after $-\otimes_{A'}K'$ (right exactness of $\otimes$). Splicing, and using $(A'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p})\otimes_{A'}K'=K'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}$, we get an exact sequence of $K'$-vector spaces $K'^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\varepsilon'}K'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{\beta}K'\otimes_{A'}\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}\to K'^{\oplus n}\to0$, $\varepsilon'(e_j)=1\otimes\mathrm da_j$, $\beta(x\otimes\mathrm da)=x\otimes\mathrm d(a\otimes1)$. Hence $\ker\beta$ is spanned by $1\otimes\mathrm da_1,\dots,1\otimes\mathrm da_n$, so $\dim\ker\beta\le n$ with equality iff these are $K'$-linearly independent, and $\dim\operatorname{coker}\beta=n$.

We conclude that the elements da_j (x) 1 generate Ker(beta)'

proof.text: *The conormal rows.* Let $(B,\mathfrak n,L)$ be a local $\mathbf F_p$-algebra; we apply this to $(A,\mathfrak m,K)$ and $(A',\mathfrak m',K')$. The Jacobi-Zariski sequence of $\mathbf F_p\to B\to L$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] is exact: $H_1(L_{L/\mathbf F_p})\to H_1(L_{L/B})\xrightarrow{\partial_B}L\otimes_B\Omega_{B/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{L/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{L/B}\to0$. Here $H_1(L_{L/\mathbf F_p})=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-h1-cotangent-vanishing], $\Omega_{L/B}=0$ and $\theta:H_1(L_{L/B})\cong\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1], and $\partial_B=\delta\circ\theta$ with $\delta(f)=1\otimes\mathrm df$ (the case $S=B$ of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-connecting-map-naturality]; there $\iota$ is the identity by [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality] (2)). Hence $0\to\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2\xrightarrow{\delta}L\otimes_B\Omega_{B/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{L/\mathbf F_p}\to0$ is exact. For $B=A$ tensor this sequence of $K$-vector spaces with $K'$ over $K$ (exact, as $K'$ is a free $K$-module): $0\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\otimes_KK'\to K'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\to K'\otimes_K\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to0$ is exact.

proof.text: *The map $\gamma$.* Let $\gamma:K'\otimes_K\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K'/\mathbf F_p}$, $x\otimes\mathrm db\mapsto x\,\mathrm db$. The Jacobi-Zariski sequence of $\mathbf F_p\to K\to K'$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence], $H_1(L_{K'/\mathbf F_p})\to H_1(L_{K'/K})\xrightarrow{\partial}K'\otimes_K\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Omega_{K'/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K'/K}\to0$, is exact and $H_1(L_{K'/\mathbf F_p})=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-field-char-p-h1-cotangent-vanishing]; so $\ker\gamma\cong H_1(L_{K'/K})$ and $\operatorname{coker}\gamma\cong\Omega_{K'/K}$. Since $K'/K$ is finite (step 3, [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-base-change-local-ring]), [lem-weil-pbc-cartier-equality] gives $\dim_{K'}\Omega_{K'/K}=\dim_{K'}H_1(L_{K'/K})<\infty$. So $\ker\gamma$ and $\operatorname{coker}\gamma$ have the same finite dimension.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular, line 8697), proof of (2) => (4) (line 8840): 'By Lemma 07E1 and the Jacobi-Zariski sequence for F_p -> K -> K' we see that the kernel and cokernel of gamma have the same finite dimension'

proof.text: *Snake lemma.* Consider the commutative diagram of $K'$-vector spaces with exact rows $0\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\otimes_KK'\to K'\otimes_A\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\to K'\otimes_K\Omega_{K/\mathbf F_p}\to0$ and $0\to\mathfrak m'/\mathfrak m'^2\to K'\otimes_{A'}\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{K'/\mathbf F_p}\to0$ (step 5) and vertical maps $\alpha$ (induced by $A\to A'$, which maps $\mathfrak m$ into $\mathfrak m'$), $\beta$ (step 4), $\gamma$ (step 6). The squares commute because $\Omega_{A/\mathbf F_p}\to\Omega_{A'/\mathbf F_p}$, $\mathrm db\mapsto\mathrm d(b\otimes1)$, is compatible with $\mathrm d$ and with the residue maps [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]: $\beta(1\otimes\mathrm df)=1\otimes\mathrm d(f\otimes1)=\delta'(\alpha(f))$ for $f\in\mathfrak m$, and $\gamma(1\otimes\mathrm d\bar b)=\mathrm d\bar b=w'(\beta(1\otimes\mathrm db))$ for $b\in A$. The snake lemma [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] gives an exact sequence $0\to\ker\alpha\to\ker\beta\to\ker\gamma\to\operatorname{coker}\alpha\to\operatorname{coker}\beta\to\operatorname{coker}\gamma\to0$ of finite-dimensional $K'$-vector spaces: $\alpha$ goes between spaces of the same dimension $d$ (steps 1, 3), so $\dim\ker\alpha=\dim\operatorname{coker}\alpha$; $\dim\ker\gamma=\dim\operatorname{coker}\gamma<\infty$ (step 6); $\dim\ker\beta\le n$, $\dim\operatorname{coker}\beta=n$ (step 4). The alternating sum of dimensions in a finite exact sequence of finite-dimensional vector spaces is $0$, so $\dim\ker\beta-\dim\operatorname{coker}\beta=(\dim\ker\alpha-\dim\operatorname{coker}\alpha)+(\dim\ker\gamma-\dim\operatorname{coker}\gamma)=0$, i.e. $\dim\ker\beta=n$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 07E5 (proposition-characterization-geometrically-regular, line 8697), proof of (2) => (4) (lines 8826-8845): the big diagram with alpha, beta, gamma; 'By assumption A' is regular ... hence the kernel and cokernel of alpha have the same dimension. It follows that the kernel and cokernel of beta have the same dimension which is what we wanted to show'

proof.text: The n vectors $1\otimes\mathrm da_i$ span $\ker\beta$, whose dimension is n by the preceding step. A spanning family of n vectors in an n-dimensional vector space is a basis, hence independent over $K\prime$. A relation with coefficients in $K$ remains such a relation after extension to $K\prime$; injectivity of the field map $K\to K\prime$ forces every coefficient to vanish. Thus the original family is independent over K. Reindexing by the chosen finite enumeration proves the assertion for I.
